title: ISM — Information Security Management
lead: A framework for protecting information assets through risk-based governance, controls and continuous improvement.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Information Security Management (ISM) provides the policies, processes and controls needed to protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information. In practice, ISM draws on standards such as ISO/IEC 27001 and NIST, and integrates with IT governance and service management to manage information risk across the organisation.

sections.heading: ITOM Perspective
sections.body: Security is a horizontal governance dimension in every IT Operating Model. ISM defines the security policies, risk appetite and control framework that constrain and guide all other operating model decisions — from architecture choices to process design and supplier management.

items.desc: Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability — the three pillars of information security.
Identifying, assessing and treating information security risks.
Technical and organisational measures to reduce security risk.
Accountability, policies and decision structures for information security.
The process for detecting, containing and recovering from security incidents.
